chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Ibn Ribat from Mansur ibn Hazim from Bakr ibn Shu'ayb said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I gave a coat to the dyer, and he took it, as he claimed. He said: If you accuse him, make him take an oath; and if you do not accuse him, there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.فَاسْتَحْلِفْهُ: Then make him take an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a custodian is accused of keeping a deposited item?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *qasam* (oath) in resolving disputes over deposited goods (*udhi'ah*), reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams in commercial transactions. It highlights the Shia legal distinction between a simple claim and a formal accusation, where the burden of proof shifts to the custodian's oath only when the depositor explicitly alleges fault, thereby protecting the custodian from arbitrary claims.
